sources.entry: hishel - RFC 9111-compliant HTTP caching for clients like httpx and requests and servers like FastAPI, with sync and async support.

summary.one_liner: Hishel is an RFC 9111-compliant HTTP caching library for Python that plugs into HTTP clients and ASGI/web frameworks, with sync and async support.
summary.what_it_does: Hishel adds HTTP response caching to Python code following the RFC 9111 caching specification. According to the README, it integrates with HTTPX, HTTPX2, Requests, ASGI applications, FastAPI, and BlackSheep, with the stated aim of minimal code changes. It supports both synchronous and asynchronous workflows. Storage is described as SQLite-backed, with more backends "coming soon". The README also mentions configurable caching policies, streaming to avoid loading large payloads into memory, and GraphQL query caching with body-sensitive content caching. The README is a short feature overview and points to external documentation for details.
use_cases: add response caching to FastAPI endpoints
reduce repeated API calls with RFC 9111 rules
cache GraphQL queries by request body
notable: Client integrations for HTTPX and Requests plus ASGI/FastAPI/BlackSheep server-side use
Streaming support to limit memory use for large payloads
caveats: Only SQLite storage is named in the README; other backends are listed as future work
README gives no install or usage commands; setup details are in external documentation
